I've now covered 16 classes (some with multiple views). Let me assess my findings:

**Test image features:**
- Two ripe orange tomatoes with large circular/sunken lesions at the blossom end
- Left tomato: advanced dark black/gray mold with concentric rings
- Right tomato: early stage — pinkish-brown ring around a darker center with gray mold
- Classic fruit rot pattern on ripe fruit

**Class comparison summary:**
- **Anthracnose** (Bugwood_1): Circular sunken lesions with dark centers on ripe red tomato — closest visual match
- **Anthracnose** (Bugwood_16): Large dark lesion on orange/ripe fruit — strong match
- Alternaria: All microscopy or stem canker images — no fruit match
- Rhizopus: Microscopy and whole-plant collapse — no match
- Gray Mold: Fluffy white mold on cracked green tomatoes — different appearance
- Sclerotinia, Southern Blight: Whole-plant wilting — no match
- Early Blight, Bacterial Speck, Bacterial Canker: Leaf symptoms — no match
- Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus: Leaf spots — no match

The circular sunken lesions on ripe tomatoes with dark mold growth (acervuli) are the defining visual signature of **Anthracnose** fruit rot (*Colletotrichum* spp.), and both macroscopic Anthracnose reference images closely match the test image.
